exercicios.enunciado: Se eu tivesse mais tempo, estudava todos os dias.

exercicios.enunciado: What would Paulo buy?

exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: "If I were you" ligado, como uma só palavra.
If you were the director of your company or school for one day, what would you change? Say three things, and why.
exercicios.frase: I'd
exercicios.resposta: If I were the director, I'd change three things. First, I'd start work at eight thirty, because the traffic is terrible at eight. Second, I'd buy new computers: ours are too slow. And I'd give everyone a free lunch on Fridays. People would be happier.

exercicios.enunciado: Would you like to be a manager one day? Why, or why not?
exercicios.frase: would
exercicios.resposta: Yes, I would. If I were a manager, I'd help my team to learn new things. But I don't think I'm ready now: I'd like two or three more years of experience first.

Talk about the next weekend: two real plans with "if" and "will", and one dream with "if" and "would".
exercicios.frase: I'd
exercicios.resposta: If the weather is good on Saturday, I'll go to the beach with my family. If my brother calls, we'll have lunch together. But if I had a boat, I'd go to Mussulo every weekend!

exercicios.enunciado: Is it better to plan for problems before they happen, or to solve them when they happen? Why?
exercicios.frase: if
exercicios.resposta: In my view, it's better to plan. If you have a plan B, you won't panic in a crisis. For example, if the internet goes down at my office, we'll use our phones. We decided that last year.

licoes.objectivo: Dizer a probabilidade com will definitely / probably, may, might, probably won't e I doubt.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: The crane [probably won't] work on the twenty-fifth.
exercicios.explicacao: probably: depois de will, antes de won't.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.
exercicios.frase: It [might] rain tomorrow.

exercicios.enunciado: Complete a frase.

exercicios.enunciado: Which sentence is the most certain?

opcoes.texto: The satellite will definitely be ready.
The satellite will probably be ready.

exercicios.enunciado: "Will Paulo come to the party?" You think no (20%). You say:
"I doubt Domingos can find another crane." Hannah thinks…
Choose the correct sentence.

opcoes.texto: It may be windy on Thursday.
It may to be windy on Thursday.

exercicios.frase: This is Hannah. The forecast says strong wind on the twenty-fifth, so the crane probably won't work that day.
exercicios.enunciado: What is the problem on the twenty-fifth?

exercicios.frase: I doubt it. The crane probably won't work.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita: em "doubt" não se diz o "b".
Talk about next year, at work or in your studies. Say two things with "will probably" or "will definitely", one with "might", and one with "I doubt".
exercicios.frase: might
exercicios.resposta: Next year I'll probably start a new project, and I'll definitely take an English exam. I might change departments — my manager asked me last week. But I doubt I'll get a pay rise: the company doesn't have enough money this year.

exercicios.enunciado: Do you trust the weather forecast? Why, or why not?
exercicios.frase: probably
exercicios.resposta: Not always. Sometimes the forecast says it'll probably rain, and then it's sunny all day! But for strong wind or big storms, I think it's quite good. So I usually check it before a trip.

Describe a delay or a shortage at your work or in your city. What caused it, and how did people sort it out?
exercicios.frase: sorted
exercicios.resposta: Last month our office ran out of paper for a week, because the supplier had a problem with a delivery. It caused a lot of problems: we couldn't print contracts. In the end, my manager sorted it out: she found a second supplier in Viana.

exercicios.enunciado: In your opinion, what causes most delays at work: documents, transport, or bad planning?
exercicios.frase: causes
exercicios.resposta: In my opinion, bad planning causes most delays. For example, people order things too late, and then the supplier runs out of stock. If we planned better, we'd have fewer problems.

licoes.titulo: Real English: What would you do?
licoes.objectivo: Identificar o problema e a solução proposta em quatro chamadas para um programa de rádio.

exercicios.frase: I'm Ricardo. My supplier ran out of brake pads two weeks ago, and I have six cars waiting.
exercicios.enunciado: How many cars are waiting at Ricardo's workshop?

exercicios.frase: This is Ricardo. Call workshops in Benguela? That might not work. They're my competitors!
exercicios.enunciado: Why doesn't Ricardo want to call workshops in Benguela?

opcoes.texto: The port is busy in August.

exercicios.enunciado: How late do Joseph's meetings start?

exercicios.enunciado: How much did the price of flour go up?

exercicios.frase: This is Fátima. Maybe I'll buy flour with two other bakeries. A bigger order is usually cheaper.
exercicios.enunciado: What is Fátima's idea?

opcoes.texto: to buy flour with two other bakeries

exercicios.enunciado: Marta says: "If I were you, I'd find a second supplier." She is…
Ricardo doesn't like an idea. What does he say?

opcoes.texto: If I were you, I'd do it.

exercicios.frase: What about ordering from a supplier in Luanda?
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.

exercicios.frase: If I raise my prices, I might lose customers.
exercicios.enunciado: Ouça e repita em voz alta.
You're the presenter. A caller says: "I start work at seven, but the bus is always late, and my boss is angry." Give two suggestions.
exercicios.frase: If I were you
exercicios.resposta: If I were you, I'd talk to your boss and explain the problem. Why don't you ask to start at seven thirty? Or what about sharing a car with a colleague? It'll probably cost a bit more than the bus, but you won't be late.

exercicios.enunciado: Which of the four problems is the most difficult to solve, in your opinion? Why?
exercicios.frase: because
exercicios.resposta: In my view, Fátima's problem is the most difficult, because she can't control the price of flour. If she raises her prices, she might lose customers. Amina's problem is easier: she can talk to her boss.

Your company needs laptops for a training on Monday. The supplier is late. Option one: wait — free, but they might arrive on Tuesday. Option two: rent laptops — they'll definitely be here, but it costs three hundred dollars. Compare the options and recommend one.
exercicios.frase: recommend
exercicios.resposta: Option one is cheaper, but it isn't as safe. The laptops might arrive on Tuesday, and the training starts on Monday. If we waited, twenty people would sit without computers for a day. Option two is more expensive, but the laptops will definitely be here. I recommend option two.

exercicios.enunciado: A foreign colleague asks about this note. Explain it in English: "Informamos que a entrega das cadeiras fica adiada para dia 20, por falta de stock. Pedimos desculpa pelo incómodo. Se preferir, podemos entregar já metade da encomenda."
exercicios.frase: It says
exercicios.resposta: It says the supplier is putting off the delivery of the chairs until the twentieth, because they don't have enough in stock. They say sorry. And if we want, they can deliver half of the order now.

If you could change one thing at your workplace, what would it be? Why?
exercicios.frase: would
exercicios.resposta: If I could change one thing, it would be the meeting room. It's too small for our team, and it's always hot. If we had a bigger room with air conditioning, our meetings would be shorter and better.

exercicios.enunciado: Your colleague says: "Let's wait for the supplier. It's cheaper." You think it's risky. Answer with a suggestion.
exercicios.frase: What about
exercicios.resposta: I see your point, but it might take two weeks. What about calling a second supplier? It'll probably cost a bit more, but we won't miss the deadline.
